preamble.summary: Chapter 24 is the theological and literary summit of the book of Sirach. Personified Wisdom delivers a magnificent self-praise, declaring her origin from the mouth of the Most High, her dwelling among all peoples, and her final settlement in Israel -- specifically in the tabernacle on Zion. She is likened to the great trees and precious spices of the land. The chapter concludes by identifying Wisdom with the Torah and comparing her instruction to overflowing rivers.
preamble.remarkable: This is one of the most theologically consequential passages in all of Jewish and Christian scripture. Wisdom's declaration 'I came forth from the mouth of the Most High' (v. 5) and 'Before the ages, in the beginning, he created me' (v. 14) became central texts in christological debates -- early Christians read these verses as prefiguring Christ as the pre-existent Word. The identification of Wisdom with the Torah (v. 32) is the definitive Sirach statement: Wisdom is not an abstract philosophical principle but is concretely embodied in the commandments of Moses. The botanical imagery (cedars, palms, roses, olives) creates a sensuous portrait of Wisdom as both beautiful and rooted.
preamble.friction: The relationship between personified Wisdom and God is theologically ambiguous: is Wisdom a created being, a divine attribute, or something else entirely? This ambiguity fueled centuries of debate in both Judaism and Christianity. The Vulgate's 'creavit me' (v. 14) -- 'he created me' -- was especially contested in Arian controversies. The claim that Wisdom 'took root in an honored people' (Israel specifically) raises questions about the universality announced in the earlier verses.
preamble.connections: Proverbs 8:22-31 (Wisdom's self-praise at creation); Job 28 (where can wisdom be found?); Baruch 3:9-4:4 (Wisdom identified with Torah); John 1:1-14 (the Word made flesh, parallel to Wisdom's incarnation in Israel); Colossians 1:15-20 (Christ as firstborn of creation).

verses.text_latin: Sapientia laudabit animam suam et in Deo honorabitur et in medio populi sui gloriabitur.
verses.rendering: Wisdom will praise her own soul, and she will be honored in God, and she will glory in the midst of her people.
translator_notes: The opening announces a unique literary form: Wisdom speaks in the first person, praising herself. This is not arrogance but revelation -- she speaks what only she can know about herself.

key_terms.rendered_as: in the midst of her people
key_terms.note: Wisdom claims Israel as 'her people' -- she is not a visitor but a permanent resident among them.

verses.text_latin: In ecclesia Altissimi aperiet os suum et in conspectu virtutis illius gloriabitur.
verses.rendering: In the assembly of the Most High she will open her mouth, and in the presence of his power she will glory.

key_terms.note: The heavenly court -- Wisdom speaks first in the divine council before her earthly manifestation.

verses.text_latin: In medio populi sui exaltabitur et in plenitudine sancta admirabitur.
verses.rendering: In the midst of her people she will be exalted, and in the holy fullness she will be admired.

verses.text_latin: In multitudine electorum habebit laudem et inter benedictos benedicetur dicens.
verses.rendering: In the multitude of the chosen she will have praise, and among the blessed she will be blessed, saying:
translator_notes: The narrative frame gives way to direct speech -- Wisdom herself now speaks.

verses.text_latin: Ego ex ore Altissimi prodii primogenita ante omnem creaturam.
verses.rendering: I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, the firstborn before all creation.
translator_notes: The most theologically charged verse in Sirach. Wisdom claims divine origin ('from the mouth of the Most High') and temporal priority over all created things. Christian tradition heard in this verse a prefiguration of the Logos of John 1:1.

key_terms.rendered_as: from the mouth of the Most High
key_terms.note: Wisdom proceeds from God's speech -- she is both word and speaker, both utterance and the one who utters. The connection to Genesis 1 ('And God said') is immediate.
Not merely first in time but first in rank -- the Greek protoktistos stands behind this, and the christological parallel to Colossians 1:15 is striking.

verses.text_latin: Ego feci in caelis ut oriretur lumen indeficiens et sicut nebula texi omnem terram.
verses.rendering: I caused an unfailing light to arise in the heavens, and like a mist I covered all the earth.
translator_notes: Wisdom's agency in creation: she is the light that fills the heavens and the mist that shrouds the earth -- both illumination and mystery.

verses.text_latin: Ego in altissimis habitavi et thronus meus in columna nubis.
verses.rendering: I dwelt in the highest places, and my throne was upon a pillar of cloud.
translator_notes: The pillar of cloud directly evokes the Exodus theophany (Exodus 13:21) -- Wisdom identifies herself with God's guiding presence.

key_terms.note: The cloud pillar of the Exodus becomes Wisdom's throne -- she is the intelligence behind God's historical guidance of Israel.

verses.text_latin: Gyrum caeli circuivi sola et profundum abyssi penetravi.
verses.rendering: I alone circled the vault of heaven and penetrated the depth of the abyss.
translator_notes: Wisdom's scope is cosmic -- from the highest heavens to the deepest abyss, she has traversed the full range of creation.

verses.text_latin: In fluctibus maris ambulavi et in omni terra steti.
verses.rendering: I walked upon the waves of the sea and stood in every land.

verses.text_latin: Et in omni populo et in omni gente primatum habui.
verses.rendering: And in every people and in every nation I held the first place.
translator_notes: Wisdom's universal sovereignty before her particular settlement in Israel.

verses.text_latin: Et omnium excellentium et humilium corda virtute calcavi et in his omnibus requiem quaesivi et in hereditate Domini morabor.
verses.rendering: And I trampled the hearts of all, the exalted and the humble, by my power; and among all these I sought rest, and in the inheritance of the Lord I will dwell.
translator_notes: The pivot: Wisdom has power over all nations but seeks rest -- a settled dwelling -- in Israel specifically.

key_terms.note: Wisdom's 'rest' parallels God's rest in creation (Genesis 2:2) and the Sabbath rest promised to Israel -- she comes home to the covenant people.

verses.text_latin: Tunc praecepit et dixit mihi Creator omnium et qui creavit me requievit in tabernaculo meo.
verses.rendering: Then the Creator of all things commanded me, and he who created me gave my tent its resting place.
translator_notes: God assigns Wisdom her dwelling -- she does not choose Israel on her own but is sent by divine decree.

key_terms.note: The tabernacle/tent directly evokes the mishkan -- the portable sanctuary where God's presence dwelt among Israel.

verses.text_latin: Et dixit mihi in Iacob inhabita et in Israhel hereditare et in electis meis mitte radices.
verses.rendering: And he said to me: 'Make your dwelling in Jacob, and in Israel take your inheritance, and among my chosen ones put down roots.'
translator_notes: The divine command is explicit: Wisdom is to settle permanently in Israel. The language of inheritance echoes the land promise.

key_terms.note: The botanical metaphor begins here -- Wisdom is not a passing visitor but a deeply rooted presence, like a great tree that will grow and bear fruit in Israel.

verses.text_latin: Ab initio et ante saecula creata sum et usque ad futurum saeculum non desinam et in habitatione sancta coram ipso ministravi.
verses.rendering: Before the ages, in the beginning, I was created, and until the age to come I will not cease; and in the holy dwelling I ministered before him.
translator_notes: The contested 'creata sum' -- was Wisdom created or eternal? The Vulgate follows the Greek ktizo, but the theological implications differ dramatically depending on whether one reads this as literal creation or as metaphorical emanation.

key_terms.note: This phrase became a battleground in the Arian controversy. Arius cited it to argue that the Son/Logos was a created being; the Nicene response distinguished between the eternal generation of the Son and the creation of the world.

verses.text_latin: Et sic in Sion firmata sum et in civitate sanctificata similiter requievi et in Hierusalem potestas mea.
verses.rendering: And so in Zion I was established, and in the holy city I likewise found rest, and in Jerusalem is my authority.
translator_notes: Wisdom's cosmic journey ends in a specific place: Zion, Jerusalem, the Temple mount. The universal becomes intensely local.

verses.text_latin: Et radicavi in populo honorificato et in parte Dei mei hereditas illius et in plenitudine sanctorum detentio mea.
verses.rendering: And I took root in an honored people, in the portion of God's own inheritance, and my abode is in the fullness of the saints.

verses.text_latin: Quasi cedrus exaltata sum in Libano et quasi cypressus in monte Hermon.
verses.rendering: I was exalted like a cedar in Lebanon, and like a cypress on Mount Hermon.
translator_notes: The botanical self-description begins: cedar and cypress are the noblest trees of the Levant.

key_terms.note: The cedar of Lebanon is the supreme symbol of majesty and endurance in the Hebrew Bible -- the tree from which Solomon built the Temple.

verses.text_latin: Quasi palma exaltata sum in Cades et quasi plantatio rosae in Hiericho.
verses.rendering: I was exalted like a palm tree in Kadesh, and like a rose planting in Jericho.

verses.text_latin: Quasi oliva speciosa in campis et quasi platanus exaltata sum iuxta aquam in plateis.
verses.rendering: Like a beautiful olive tree in the plains, and like a plane tree I was exalted beside water in the open places.

key_terms.note: The olive is the most economically and symbolically important tree of the Mediterranean -- oil, light, anointing, and peace all flow from it.

verses.text_latin: Sicut cinnamomum et aspaltum aromatizans odorem dedi quasi myrrha electa dedi suavitatem odoris.
verses.rendering: Like cinnamon and fragrant balm I gave forth aroma; like choice myrrh I gave sweetness of fragrance.
translator_notes: From trees to spices: Wisdom is not only majestic but intoxicatingly fragrant -- her presence is sensed before it is seen.

verses.text_latin: Et quasi storax et galbanus et ungula et gutta et quasi Libanus non incisus vaporavi habitationem meam et quasi balsamum non mixtum odor meus.
verses.rendering: Like storax and galbanum and onycha and stacte, and like Lebanon incense uncut, I perfumed my dwelling; and my fragrance is like unmixed balsam.
translator_notes: The spice list echoes the sacred incense recipe of Exodus 30:34 -- Wisdom's perfume is temple incense.

key_terms.note: Uncut frankincense -- the purest form before processing. Wisdom's fragrance is raw and undiluted.

verses.text_latin: Ego quasi terebinthus extendi ramos meos et rami mei honoris et gratiae.
verses.rendering: I stretched out my branches like a terebinth, and my branches are branches of glory and grace.

verses.text_latin: Ego quasi vitis fructificavi suavitatem odoris et flores mei fructus honoris et honestatis.
verses.rendering: I bore fruit like a vine with the sweetness of fragrance, and my blossoms are the fruit of honor and uprightness.

verses.text_latin: Ego mater pulchrae dilectionis et timoris et agnitionis et sanctae spei.
verses.rendering: I am the mother of beautiful love, and of fear, and of knowledge, and of holy hope.
translator_notes: Wisdom as 'mother' -- she generates the cardinal virtues of the moral life: love, fear of God, knowledge, and hope.

key_terms.note: A title that later Catholic tradition applied to the Virgin Mary, reading Sirach 24 as a Marian text.

verses.text_latin: In me gratia omnis viae et veritatis in me omnis spes vitae et virtutis.
verses.rendering: In me is all grace of the way and of truth; in me is all hope of life and of virtue.

verses.text_latin: Transite ad me omnes qui concupiscitis me et a generationibus meis implemini.
verses.rendering: Come to me, all you who desire me, and be filled with my fruits.
translator_notes: Wisdom's invitation -- open to all who desire her. The echo of this verse in Matthew 11:28 ('Come to me, all you who labor') is striking.

verses.text_latin: Spiritus enim meus super mel dulcis et hereditas mea super mel et favum.
verses.rendering: For my spirit is sweeter than honey, and my inheritance surpasses honey and the honeycomb.

key_terms.note: Echoes Psalm 19:10 where God's ordinances are 'sweeter than honey' -- Wisdom and Torah share the same sweetness.

verses.text_latin: Memoria mea in generationes saeculorum.
verses.rendering: My memory endures through the generations of the ages.

verses.text_latin: Qui edunt me adhuc esurient et qui bibunt me adhuc sitient.
verses.rendering: Those who eat me will hunger for more, and those who drink me will thirst for more.
translator_notes: A paradox of satisfaction: Wisdom satisfies yet creates deeper longing. Jesus reverses this in John 6:35 ('whoever comes to me will never hunger') -- the contrast is theologically significant.

verses.text_latin: Qui audit me non confundetur et qui operantur in me non peccabunt.
verses.rendering: Whoever listens to me will not be put to shame, and those who labor with me will not sin.

verses.text_latin: Qui elucidant me vitam aeternam habebunt.
verses.rendering: Those who illuminate me will have eternal life.
translator_notes: A momentous claim: those who make Wisdom shine forth -- who teach and embody her -- receive the gift of eternal life.

key_terms.note: One of the earliest explicit promises of eternal life in Jewish literature, anticipating the full development of this concept in later apocalyptic and New Testament writings.

verses.text_latin: Haec omnia liber vitae et testamentum Altissimi et agnitio veritatis.
verses.rendering: All these things are the book of life, the covenant of the Most High, and the knowledge of truth.
translator_notes: The decisive identification: everything Wisdom has said about herself is in fact a description of the Torah -- the book of life, God's covenant, the source of truth.

key_terms.note: The Torah is the 'book of life' -- not merely a legal code but the written form of Wisdom herself, the source of existence.
Testamentum here means covenant (diatheke in Greek) -- the Torah is the documentary expression of God's binding relationship with Israel.

verses.text_latin: Legem mandavit Moses in praeceptis iustitiarum hereditatem domui Iacob et Israhel promissiones.
verses.rendering: Moses commanded the law as precepts of justice, an inheritance for the house of Jacob, and promises to Israel.
translator_notes: The transition from personified Wisdom to historical Torah is now complete: what Wisdom proclaimed in the first person, Moses codified as law.

verses.text_latin: Posuit David puero suo excitare regem ex ipso fortissimum et in throno honoris sedentem in sempiternum.
verses.rendering: He made a promise to David his servant to raise up from him a most mighty king, sitting on the throne of honor forever.
translator_notes: A brief but significant Davidic messianic reference within the Wisdom discourse.

verses.text_latin: Qui implet quasi Phison sapientiam et sicut Tigris in diebus novorum.
verses.rendering: He who fills with wisdom like the Pishon, and like the Tigris in the days of new things.
translator_notes: The four rivers of Eden (Genesis 2:10-14) become metaphors for the overflowing abundance of Torah-Wisdom.

key_terms.note: One of the four rivers of Eden -- Torah-Wisdom flows from paradise, suggesting that obedience restores access to the garden.

verses.text_latin: Qui adimplet quasi Eufrates sensum qui multiplicat quasi Iordanis in tempore messis.
verses.rendering: He who fills understanding like the Euphrates, who multiplies it like the Jordan at harvest time.

verses.text_latin: Qui mittit disciplinam sicut lucem et adsistens quasi Geon in die vindimiae.
verses.rendering: He who sends forth instruction like light, standing by like the Gihon in the day of vintage.

verses.text_latin: Qui perficit primus scire ipsam et infirmior non investigabit eam.
verses.rendering: The first man did not finish knowing her, nor will the last one fathom her.
translator_notes: Neither Adam (the first man) nor the final generation will exhaust Wisdom -- she is inexhaustible.

verses.text_latin: A mari enim abundavit cogitatio eius et consilium illius ab abysso magna.
verses.rendering: For her thought overflows from the sea, and her counsel from the great abyss.

verses.text_latin: Ego sapientia effudi flumina.
verses.rendering: I, Wisdom, have poured forth rivers.
translator_notes: Wisdom resumes first-person speech for a final declaration of her creative power.

verses.text_latin: Ego quasi trames aquae inmensae de fluvio ego quasi fluvii dioryx et sicut aquaeductus exivi de paradiso.
verses.rendering: I am like a channel from a vast river, like a watercourse, and like an aqueduct I came forth from paradise.

key_terms.note: Wisdom's origin is Eden itself -- she is the living water that flows from the primordial garden into the world.

verses.text_latin: Dixi rigabo hortum meum plantationum et inebriabo prati mei fructum.
verses.rendering: I said, 'I will water my garden of plantings, and I will drench the fruit of my meadow.'

verses.text_latin: Et ecce factus est mihi trames abundans et fluvius meus adpropinquavit ad mare.
verses.rendering: And behold, my channel became a river, and my river drew near to the sea.
translator_notes: The image of ever-expanding water: Wisdom's influence grows from channel to river to ocean.

verses.text_latin: Quoniam doctrinam quasi antelucanum inlumino omnibus et enarrabo illam usque ad longinquum.
verses.rendering: For I make instruction shine like the dawn for all, and I will proclaim it to the farthest places.

key_terms.note: The light before sunrise -- Wisdom illuminates before the full day, preparing the world for understanding.

verses.text_latin: Penetrabo omnes inferiores partes terrae et inspiciam omnes dormientes et inluminabo omnes sperantes in Domino.
verses.rendering: I will penetrate all the lower parts of the earth, and I will look upon all who sleep, and I will illumine all who hope in the Lord.
translator_notes: Wisdom's reach extends even to Sheol -- the sleeping dead are not beyond her gaze. Her final act is to bring light to those who hope.

verses.text_latin: Adhuc doctrinam quasi prophetiam effundam et relinquam illam quaerentibus sapientiam et non desinam in progenies illorum usque in aevum sanctum.
verses.rendering: I will yet pour out instruction like prophecy, and I will leave it to those who seek wisdom, and I will not cease for their descendants until the holy age.
translator_notes: The final verse: Wisdom promises perpetual instruction -- she will never stop teaching, generation after generation, until the eschatological consummation.

key_terms.note: An eschatological horizon -- Wisdom's instruction continues until the final age, the fulfillment of all things.
